mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE < 5% for two consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1 falling for two consecutive quarters) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of two consecutive quarterly GDPC1 declines (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO falling for three consecutive months) signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and suppresses earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO falls for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS rising by more than 200,000 in a single month) during a period of elevated unemployment (UNRATE > 6%) signals a nascent recovery, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate sales, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS jumps >200,000 and UNRATE > 6% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above the previous 12-month average for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during four consecutive months of above-average HOUST (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal savings (RSAFS falling for five consecutive months) indicates increased consumer reliance on credit, which can amplify demand but also raise default risk, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days if accompanied by rising consumer spending proxies.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during five consecutive months of declining RSAFS (t-test p > 0.05).
